sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (annual, sick, emergency, etc.) — used in every leave request and balance query join; is_active: filter active leave types for dropdowns and policy assignment

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join with leave_types for policy lookups during leave request validation; is_active: filter active policies for request eligibility checks

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups — employee views own requests, manager views team requests; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type for reporting; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager retrieves their approval history

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: primary access pattern — employee checks own balance, manager checks team balances; employee_id, leave_type_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup for balance deduction during leave approval; fiscal_year: annual balance reset queries

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique login lookup; manager_id: manager retrieves direct reports for team leave views and approval queues; employment_status: filter active employees for leave eligibility; deleted_at: soft-delete filter on all queries

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, ip_address, user_agent, performed_at, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookup for a specific entity (e.g. all changes to leave_request #42); performed_by: audit by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filter by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE, etc.)
data_notes: Persistence slice defined with 6 conceptual table specs and 6 repository interfaces. Tables: leave_types, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, employees, audit_logs. All repositories backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts. Audit table (audit_logs) satisfies GP-002 — every state-changing operation writes here. Employees table includes manager_id self-referencing FK for RBAC manager hierarchy (GP-005). Leave balances use composite unique on (employee_id, leave_type_id, fiscal_year) for accurate deduction tracking.
